description:
RFC 9553 §1.4.5 defines UTCDateTime as 'a string in the form defined in
[RFC3339], section 5.6 with the time-offset always being "Z".' Two fields in
this crate carry that type:

- Timestamp.utc at lib.rs:933 (mandatory, RFC 9553 §2.8.1)
- Note.created at lib.rs:1043 (optional, RFC 9553 §2.8.3)

Both are typed bare String. A caller can construct Timestamp { utc:
"not a date".into(), ... } and round-trip it through serde. No parse helper,
no validation, no FromStr-into-chrono path documented. Every consumer that
actually needs the date value reaches for chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339
or time::OffsetDateTime::parse separately.

Two reasonable fixes:

(a) Add a UTCDateTime newtype around String with a validating constructor
    (UTCDateTime::new(s: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, ParseError>) and a
    method that returns the parsed value via chrono or time on a feature flag.
(b) Keep String but document the parse contract explicitly in the doc comment
    and add an example of the right way to parse.

Option (a) introduces a chrono-or-time dep behind a feature flag, which the
crate's design constraints currently forbid (serde + serde_json only). Option
(b) is zero-cost and resolves the contract gap.

This is the analog of jmap-types::UTCDate — that type is also a String newtype,
so the workspace convention is closer to (b). At minimum, add the doc clause.
title: UTCDateTime fields typed as String — no parse contract, no validation, no chrono/time type
